title: Poilievre heading to Washington next week in push for tariff-free trade with U.S.
summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is heading to Washington next week as trade talks between Canada and the United States continue.

image.caption: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre will be heading to the U.S. capital next week. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is heading to Washington next week as trade talks between Canada and the United States continue.
Poilievre gave Prime Minister's Office a heads-up about his trip, source says
· Posted: Nov 27, 2026 1:39 PM EST | Last Updated: 14 minutes ago

A senior Conservative source speaking to The Canadian Press on background says Poilievre will be in the U.S. capital on Dec. 3 for a fireside chat at an International Democracy Union conference and to deliver a speech at the Canadian American Business Council.
The source says Poilievre has given the Prime Minister's Office a heads-up about his trip and has spoken with Ambassador to the U.S. Mark Wiseman, who offered to brief him before the visit.

Poilievre is very open to meetings with politicians but is waiting to co-ordinate with the Prime Minister's Office, says the source, adding that it's unlikely the leader will meet with anyone from the Trump administration.

items: Poilievre tells U.S. TV Canadians are 'wounded' and 'confused' to be in America's crosshairs

blocks.text: Poilievre said in a statement he will be travelling to Washington to make the case for tariff-free trade with the United States to protect Canadian jobs and bring down the cost of living.
U.S. President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada rapidly escalated after negotiations broke down in August. Both sides have said that talks picked up over the last month.
Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said Wednesday that Ottawa expects trade talks to continue next week.
Catherine Morrison is a reporter for The Canadian Press.
